analyzed_vuln.description: In the kCommandPredict branch, UnpredictICC decodes `num` with DecodeVarInt and only checks `CheckOutOfBounds(pos, num, size)` against total input size, but then reads bytes from `enc[pos + i]` in a loop without ensuring `pos + num` stays within the command section boundary (`commands_end`). Because command bytes and payload share one buffer and `commands_end` can be smaller than `size`, this allows reading past the allocated fuzzer input when `num` is attacker-controlled, causing a 1-byte heap OOB read at `shuffled[i] = enc[pos + i]` (line ~287).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via icc_codec_fuzzer read mode (first byte 0), attacker-controlled compressed ICC data reaches UnpredictICC. The input must make parsing enter kCommandPredict and provide a varint `num` large enough that payload copy uses bytes beyond available input/command partition; existing checks do not constrain this against `commands_end` before the copy loop. The provided PoC triggers exactly this path and causes read at the end of the heap buffer.
